clue.text: Extra time again?

definitions.meaning: one more go or occasion, as in 'try it one more time'

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves define the phrase: extra time is one more occasion, and 'again' is its everyday synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a further occasion, so it serves both as 'extra time' and as a synonym of 'again'.

clue.text: Try to turn crazy

indicators.note: to turn tells us to read the word for crazy from right to left

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy or mad

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to go mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses BATS, the slang word for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a try at it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Elizabeth's boy catcher

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
a net is used to catch fish or butterflies

explanation.surface: A young lad belonging to Elizabeth catches things.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth is the heroine of Pride and Prejudice, whose surname this is; 'Elizabeth's' therefore stands for her family name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Bennet is Jane Austen's heroine, so her surname is what belongs to Elizabeth in literary terms.

clue.text: 10 sounds far from sweet

indicators.note: sounds says the herb's name is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: the cross-reference is to 10, HERB; savory is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A herb that is said to taste anything but sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is HERB: the herb savory, spelt without a U, is spoken aloud to give the word for salty or non-sweet food.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoury food is salty or spicy rather than sweet, the opposite of a dessert taste.

clue.text: Unable to forget love, Elizabeth retains second 17

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: retains means the short name holds another piece inside it

parts.note: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth
17 is EDITION, abbreviated ed.

explanation.surface: Elizabeth, in love, keeps a second version of something she cannot let go of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts S inside the pet name, and O for love is the tennis zero; 17 is the cross-reference to EDITION, whose usual abbreviation supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed is fixated, quite unable to put a thought out of mind.

clue.text: One like St Francis with optical problem

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a
St Francis of Assisi bore the stigmata, the wounds of Christ, so he was stigmatic

explanation.surface: A saintly figure resembling Francis of Assisi who has trouble with his eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: A stigmatic is a person bearing the stigmata, as St Francis famously did.
explanation.definitionFit: Astigmatism is a defect of the eye's lens or cornea causing blurred vision, an optical fault.

clue.text: Star is taken from boy

indicators.note: taken from says the word is removed out of the name

parts.note: Alistair is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A celebrity being removed from a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes IS from ALISTAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Extracts from a national anthem are what I can't abide

annotationWithheld.why: Extracts from a national anthem are what I can't abide (8): pieces A, NAT, HEM and a final A cannot be taken from 'a national anthem' in answer order, so no parse gives the letters without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Extracts from a national anthem are what I can't abide

clue.text: 10 boy

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is HERB; the word is both a kitchen herb and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb used in Italian cooking and also a man's given name.

clue.text: Plant for 3, say, or her brother

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run on in the clue's words is a coincidence, not a hidden word
B is an abbreviation for brother; the letters also running on in the clue's words is a coincidence of this charade, not a hiding

explanation.surface: A plant used for a neighbour, or the brother of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is BENNET, and herb bennet is a wild plant, so the word is what goes before 3 in a plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb bennet, or wood avens, is a wild plant whose name begins with this word.

clue.text: Modern note struck by 23 and others

indicators.note: struck suggests the note is hit and knocked out of order

parts.note: 23 is ERIC COATES, whose first name gives these letters
et al. is Latin for and others, giving al

explanation.surface: A new musical note played by a composer and others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' rearranges NOTE as NEOT; ERIC comes from 23, ERIC COATES, and AL from et al.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoterical is a rare word meaning recent or newly invented, from Greek neoteros, newer.

clue.text: Boy after 10

definitions.meaning: herb ... is a wild geranium, so the word follows HERB

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is HERB; herb Robert is a common wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert is a boy's name and also the second word of herb Robert, a wild cranesbill.

clue.text: Fruity food in piece of church soap, possibly

parts.note: Eccles, from Greek ecclesia, is a word for church
soap is sold in cakes, so a piece of soap is a cake

explanation.surface: Some fruity treat found in a bar of church soap.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eccles cake is a round pastry filled with currants, from Eccles near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a flaky pastry filled with currants, a fruity English teatime food.

clue.text: 10 girl or girls

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl or several girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is HERB. The answer is one girl's name, or two girls' names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic evergreen herb used in cooking, especially with lamb.

clue.text: Acceptance speech to shellfish — I'm not sure …

indicators.note: speech means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: a whelk is an edible sea snail, and um is a hesitant noise of doubt; said together they make the sound

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly addressing a shellfish as they accept an award.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying WHELK then UM aloud gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome is a reception or acceptance, as when a proposal receives a warm welcome.

clue.text: 10 girl docked both ways with little girl at centre

indicators.note: at centre puts the small name in the middle of the others

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name; docked, with its tail cut off, it leaves mar

indicators.note: both ways means the cut name is also read backwards

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name; docked, with its tail cut off, it leaves mar
Jo is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl with her tail cut off, read backwards and forwards with a small girl in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the last letter off the name; 'both ways' reads the result forwards then backwards, and 'at centre' puts the short name in the middle, making a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is a sweet aromatic herb related to oregano.

clue.text: Version of antigovernment activity without leader

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: sedition is conduct inciting rebellion against the state

explanation.surface: A form of rebellion against the government that has no head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' drops the S of SEDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one version of a published work, such as a revised second edition.

clue.text: No rare Shakespearean bawd

definitions.meaning: describes meat cooked too long, the opposite of rare
Mistress ... is the brothel-keeper in Measure for Measure

explanation.walkthrough: Mistress Overdone runs a brothel in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcooked meat is the opposite of rare, and Mistress Overdone is Shakespeare's bawd.

clue.text: Synthetic fibre makes the best pictures

parts.note: ace means first-rate or best
the Tate is the London art gallery, full of pictures

explanation.surface: An artificial textile produces the finest paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in London and elsewhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a man-made fibre made from cellulose acetate.

clue.text: High-speed (ascent in metaphor, descent in reality?)

definitions.meaning: rapid, like a sudden rise to fame

definitions.text: ascent in metaphor, descent in reality?
definitions.meaning: a dazzling rise to fame is likened to a shooting star, yet actual shooting stars fall

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a career's rapid rise is named after objects that fall from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteoric means very rapid, like a meteor; the irony is that real meteors fall rather than rise.

clue.text: Hanging is well prefixed here

indicators.note: prefixed means the word for well comes before the word for hanging

parts.note: eu- is a Greek prefix meaning well, as in euphoria
the rope is the instrument of hanging

explanation.surface: Execution is preceded by something well chosen here.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek prefix eu- (well) goes in front of ROPE; 'here' is the continent where the clue is read.
explanation.definitionFit: For a British setter and reader the continent is where we are, so 'here' points to it.

clue.text: Boy and version of one of 23, say

parts.note: Jack is a boy's name
the French version of and is et

explanation.surface: A lad and another version of a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is ERIC COATES, whose surname suggests coats; a jacket is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is a short coat, so it is one of the coats that 23's surname suggests.

clue.text: Boy 10, say, at 11th hour

parts.note: Justin is a boy's name

indicators.note: say signals that the herb's name is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: 10 is HERB: thyme is a herb

explanation.surface: A boy brings a herb at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is HERB; THYME is said aloud to give TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in time means at the last possible moment, which is what the eleventh hour signifies.

clue.text: Composer of piccolo part in Easter work

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
work suggests the letters are worked into a new order
part means only a section of the instrument's name is taken

explanation.surface: A composer writes a piccolo passage in an Easter piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges the festival into ERATES; 'part' takes a run from the middle of piccolo; 'in' puts that run inside. Eric Coates wrote light orchestral music.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Coates was an English composer of light music such as the Dam Busters March.

clue.text: No waiter with 24 down back in 17

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
in means the letters are found inside the word

parts.note: 17 is EDITION

explanation.surface: A time-pressed figure who will not wait, found in reverse in a version.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'time and tide wait for no man'. 'in' takes EDIT from 17, EDITION; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide, with time, is proverbially the thing that waits for no man.

clue.text: See 22
Genuine wrinkle for listener

indicators.note: for listener says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to pucker is to wrinkle or crease

explanation.surface: A real crease, as heard by someone listening.
explanation.walkthrough: PUKKA, Anglo-Indian for genuine, sounds like PUCKER in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka is Anglo-Indian slang for real, authentic or first-class.

clue.text: Singular accompaniment to roast joint taken neat by Campbell

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy
Ming was the nickname of Sir Menzies Campbell, the Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A roast is served with something neat taken by a man called Campbell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' because the trimmings of a roast are usually plural. Menzies Campbell, a British politician, was nicknamed Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: The trimmings are the side dishes served with a roast, and one of them is a trimming.
